reading.body:
Box has built a portfolio of integrations that let AI agents handle real-world tasks: sending physical mail, managing cloud files, accessing bank data, and exchanging secrets between agents.

These Model Context Protocol tools sit at the boundary between AI systems and the infrastructure they need to operate at scale. An AI agent that can only think cannot process a loan application or onboard an employee. It must read files, verify identity, send documents, and maintain audit trails. Box's integrations bridge this gap by giving agents standardized access to storage, communication channels, and cross-agent coordination. The company's own AI product focuses on enterprise content, but this MCP registry strategy positions it as an operational layer for agentic workflows, where the binding constraint shifts from model capability to the ability to act on real data and systems.

What these integrations do not show is compute or power consumption. They are software abstractions that assume infrastructure exists elsewhere. They do show that AI scaling now depends not only on larger models and more training compute, but on standardized ways for agents to access the human-world interfaces they need to do work. For enterprises, this means the grid constraint on AI is mediated through the systems that connect agents to email, filesystems, banks, and each other.

profile_text.body:
Box is an AI-powered content management and workflow platform founded in 2005 and headquartered in Redwood City, California. The company describes its offering as intelligent content management that enables users to automate workflows, collaborate internally and externally, and protect sensitive data on a single platform. Box positions itself around unstructured data—sales presentations, contracts, handbooks—allowing teams to access, share, edit, and co-create content while maintaining enterprise-grade security and compliance.

Box AI is the company's core AI product, which integrates leading AI models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google to provide real-time summaries, deep analysis, and smart recommendations from enterprise content. The platform includes workflow automation via a drag-and-drop builder and AI agents for tasks like loan processing and employee onboarding, as well as AI-driven security with malware detection, threat mitigation, and automated classification. Box also offers AI-powered e-signature workflows and compliance tools for standards including GDPR, HIPAA, and FINRA.

Box is a public company (ticker BOX, CIK 0001372612) with reported revenue of 1.177 billion USD for the fiscal year ending January 31, 2026. The company maintains significant legal exposure in California, with 208 tracked cases. Box also operates multiple Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers enabling AI agent integration with email, cloud storage, banking, and physical mail systems through the Smithery registry.
